Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

North Surrey has two main groups of condo buildings, City Centre and Guildford, and they feel quite different. I help you pick between them, then read the strata records with you before you firm up. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 and I'm in the top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors, with more than $500M in sales. I'm also proud of 10 straight years in the FVREB Medallion Club.

In Paragon, the MLS® system local REALTORS® use, North Surrey is its own area with eight sub-areas. The feed above is limited to apartment-style condos across all of them. Below it, you'll find how the condo neighbourhoods differ, how transit reaches each one, and what to read in the strata records before you buy.

City Centre is where most of the towers are, clustered around three Expo Line stations. The City's City Centre Plan aims for a walkable, transit-focused downtown, and its update allows more building near the stations. For City Centre alone, see
Whalley condos for sale
Guildford
Guildford sits east of City Centre, with Guildford Exchange and the Guildford Recreation Centre near its middle. It has the other main group of
condo buildings
in North Surrey, along with townhomes and houses. See my
Guildford homes for sale
page for every home type there.

Bolivar Heights, just north of City Centre, has a few apartment buildings, and the City Centre Plan update allows more growth there. Fraser Heights, Cedar Hills and Bridgeview are mostly detached houses, so condos there are rare. See my
Bolivar Heights homes for sale
page for that area.

Three Expo Line stations serve Whalley: Gateway, Surrey Central and King George. Guildford relies on buses from Guildford Exchange. The Province is building the Surrey Langley SkyTrain, which extends the Expo Line from King George Station along Fraser Highway to Langley City. If you plan to commute by transit, start with buildings closest to a station or exchange.

City Centre Library is on University Drive, close to Surrey Central Station. In Guildford, the Guildford Library at 15105 105 Avenue is beside the Guildford Recreation Centre. Holland Park on Old Yale Road is City Centre's big green space, about 10 hectares.

Kwantlen Park Secondary serves much of Whalley. Guildford Park Secondary and Johnston Heights Secondary serve Guildford. Condo catchments follow the building's address, so check it in the Surrey Schools School Locator.

The Guildford Plan, approved in October 2023, covers about 515 hectares around Guildford Centre. The City Centre Plan is under review. Either one can change what gets built across the street from your condo.

blocks.text: What you own when you buy a condo

parts.t: Buying a condo in BC means buying a strata lot. Your unit is yours, and you share ownership of the common property with every other owner: the roof, hallways, elevators, parkade and grounds. The strata corporation looks after it through an elected council that sets the fees and the bylaws. Items like a balcony or a parking stall may be limited common property, kept for one unit. The strata plan shows which ones go with yours.

The Province describes the Form B: Information Certificate as the strata's disclosure document for a unit. Owners, buyers or their agents can ask for it, and the strata has to hand it over within 7 days. It lists the monthly fee, any amount the seller owes, approved special levies and the reserve fund balance, with the budget, rules and latest depreciation report attached.

Stratas with five or more lots in BC need a depreciation report every five years, and they can no longer skip it with a 3/4 vote. In Surrey, a building that size should generally have a current one. It projects 30 years of repair and replacement costs. Compare it with the reserve fund on the Form B, and if there's no report attached, ask the strata why.

blocks.text: Before you buy a North Surrey condo

parts.t: Get the Form B and read the budget, the rules and the depreciation report attached to it.
Ask for two years of council and AGM minutes, plus the bylaws.
Check the strata plan for your stall and locker.
Read the pet bylaws before you fall for a unit.

blocks.text: Which North Surrey neighbourhoods have condos?

parts.t: Most North Surrey condos are in Whalley and Guildford. Bolivar Heights, Fraser Heights, Cedar Hills and Bridgeview have only a few apartment buildings.

blocks.text: How is this page different from the Whalley condos page?

parts.t: This page shows apartment-style condos in every North Surrey sub-area. The Whalley condos page shows only Whalley, which takes in Surrey City Centre.

blocks.text: Which SkyTrain stations serve North Surrey condos?

parts.t: Gateway, Surrey Central and King George Expo Line stations are in Whalley. Guildford relies on buses from Guildford Exchange.

blocks.text: What if the Form B shows no depreciation report?

parts.t: Stratas with five or more lots can no longer defer the report by a 3/4 vote, so a Surrey building that size is generally required to have a current one. If the Form B doesn't include one, ask the strata why.
The strata fee, any amount owed, approved special levies and the reserve fund balance, with the budget, rules and depreciation report attached.

blocks.text: Where are the libraries near North Surrey condos?

parts.t: City Centre Library on University Drive and Guildford Library at 15105 105 Avenue.
